summary: Edwards' PROGRESS trial cut death or heart-failure events by 33% with early valve replacement in moderate aortic stenosis.
Analysts called PROGRESS a potential market expander, but TAVR patients had slightly higher two-year mortality.
Medtronic's real-world renal denervation study in 594 patients met its endpoint and won an FDA label update.
Abbott's Amulet 360 closed the left atrial appendage in 96.3% of patients, strengthening it against Boston Scientific's Watchman.

items.title: PROGRESS trial, SAPIEN 3 transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in moderate aortic stenosis (Edwards Lifesciences)
lines: Death or heart failure (HF) event at 2 years: 16.7% vs 23.9% with surveillance; hazard ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.02, n=744.
HF events 10.8% vs 19.0%, hazard ratio 0.55, p=0.002; HF hospitalization 7.4% vs 14.9%.
All-cause mortality at 2 years 8.4% TAVR vs 7.3% surveillance; Truist flagged possible initial investor concern.
57% of surveillance patients needed a delayed valve replacement within 2 years; quality-of-life score up 15.5 points at 30 days.

items.title: SPYRAL AFFIRM, Symplicity Spyral radiofrequency renal denervation for uncontrolled hypertension (Medtronic)
lines: FDA-required single-arm post-approval study, n=594 US patients; met primary blood-pressure endpoint versus a performance goal; mmHg reduction figures not reported in sources I opened.
Diverse population: 45% women, 27% Black, 11% Hispanic, 19% with type 2 diabetes.
Nearly 9 in 10 patients had at least 10 mmHg office systolic drop, at least 5 mmHg home drop and one fewer medication.
FDA approved a label update adding clinical data; device first approved late 2023.

items.title: VERITAS pivotal study, Amulet 360 left atrial appendage (LAA) occluder (Abbott)
lines: Complete LAA closure on transesophageal echocardiography in 96.3% of patients at 1 year; patient count not reported.
Ischemic stroke or systemic embolism 1.8%; all-cause mortality 3.9%; cardiovascular mortality 1.9%; major bleeding 6.6%.
Europe's CE mark granted in August 2026; under FDA review; BTIG sees better competition with Boston Scientific's market-leading Watchman.

items.title: Ultrasound renal denervation abstracts, Paradise system (Recor Medical, Otsuka Holdings subsidiary)
lines: Seven Recor-sponsored abstracts at TCT 2026 on ultrasound renal denervation; outcome figures not reported.
Cardiovascular Business called real-world renal denervation benefit a hot topic of the meeting; figures not reported.

items.title: CLASP II TR tricuspid repair (PASCAL) and ENCIRCLE transcatheter mitral valve replacement (SAPIEN M3) (Edwards Lifesciences)
lines: CLASP II TR randomized results presented for an already FDA-approved tricuspid therapy; endpoint figures not reported.
ENCIRCLE 2-year mitral valve replacement outcomes published with JACC journals; figures not reported.

items.title: TRANSFORM II, sirolimus-coated balloon vs drug-eluting stent in native coronaries (Concept Medical, private)
lines: Late-breaking randomized trial; primary endpoint accepted by The Lancet; effect size figures not reported.
Drug-coated balloon theme also included the 3-year SIRONA trial (sirolimus vs paclitaxel balloons, leg arteries); figures not reported.

items.title: P4 trial, coronary CT angiography-guided vs intravascular ultrasound-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (investigator trial, no sponsor identified)
lines: CT guidance matched intravascular-ultrasound guidance on 1-year clinical outcomes with shorter procedures; hazard ratio and patient numbers not reported.
Presented in the Sunday coronary late-breaking session run with The Lancet; figures not reported.

expert_minds: Treating aortic stenosis earlier: Philippe Genereux called PROGRESS a turning point; J.P. Morgan reported a very strong round of applause.
TAVR market expansion: Stifel said PROGRESS could change when valve disease is treated; J.P. Morgan sees a new standard of care.
Real-world renal denervation was a hot topic per Cardiovascular Business, backed by Medtronic and Recor data.
Coronary late-breakers centred on drug-coated balloons and CT-guided PCI planning, per TCTMD and CRF late-breaker lists.
